params.body:
## Why

Under a make, the Model list on the vehicle sheet showed the same name twice (Audi A1 to A6, Peugeot 207, 208, 3008, 306), and trims were listed as models (3008 GT, 208 GTi). A dealer searching the shared stock for 3008 did not see cars filed under the other 3008 row or under 3008 GT; the public API facets and filters work per model id, so dealer websites had the same gap.

## Cause

The classic sheet loaded models through `getAllModels` (`OwnStockController::populateAllModels`) with `active = 1`, and its edit path filtered on active too. The Livewire sheet builds the list in `VehicleForm::render` without that condition, so switched-off rows came back, among them duplicates in the shape the old `models:deleteDuplicates` left behind (vehicles moved to the first row, the others set to `active = 0, models = 0` but never removed). Whether that command ever ran on production was not checked from here; the "every name exactly twice" pattern fits it. The Hexon model import also compared names literally, so a name with extra inner spacing became a second model.

## What changes

- **Sheet:** only active models are offered (R S1-3.2 already promised this), plus the vehicle's own model so opening and saving never empties it. A vehicle on a merged model opens on the model it went into.
- **`stocklist:merge-duplicate-models`** (dry run unless `--apply`, one transaction per group):
  - default: rows of one make and type whose names only differ in case or spacing merge into the row with the **most live vehicles**; on a tie, the row external mappings lean on (RealGarant code, system code, Hexon flag, rows in `real_garant_codes` and `modix_models`), then the active one, then the oldest. The survivor inherits a RealGarant or system code it lacked, is switched on if any row of the group was, and loses stray spaces.
  - `--fold-trims`: a model that is another model of the same make plus only trim words (GT, GTi, GT Line, RS, AMG, ...) folds into that base model. Each vehicle gets the base model and the trim in front of its trim field, unless the field already names it as a word. Body styles (SW, CC, Sportback, allroad, Tourer, ...) stay models. An unknown suffix, a base that exists twice, or a trim field that would pass 255 characters is listed as "needs a person" and left untouched. `--list-trims` prints the list and never writes; `--except=<id>` skips a row.
  - References repointed: `vehicles.model_id` (soft-deleted rows included), `transport.model_id`, `real_garant_codes.model_id`, `modix_models.model_id`, `vehicle_default_dimension.model_id` (a year the survivor already has stays on the retired row instead of colliding with the unique key). Writes use the query builder, so the vehicle observer and partner webhooks do not fire for every repointed vehicle.
  - Idempotent: retired rows are never grouped again.
- **Retired rows are kept**, switched off, with `models.merged_into_id` and `models.folded_trim` (new migration). Partners hold model ids; `Vehicle::booted` sends any vehicle saved on a retired id to the surviving model with the folded trim, so the next import cannot split a model again.
- **Hexon import** matches names without case or spacing, against every row of the make including retired ones.
- `models:deleteDuplicates` is removed; the new command replaces it.

Rules R S1-3.22 (one model per name per make) and R S1-3.23 (a trim is not a model); resolves bevinding: de-modellenlijst-toont-uitgeschakelde-modellen.

## Tests

`MergeDuplicateModelsTest`, `ModelNamesTest`, `VehicleFormModelListTest` (fails without the `active` filter). Full suite green locally.

## After merge

The migration runs with the deploy. The data changes only when the command is run with `--apply`; the dry run lists every group and every trim with vehicle counts first.
params.title: One model per name per make, and a trim is not a model
